brand_identity.name: The Whole Truth Foods
brand_identity.tagline: We're re-building the world's trust in food.
brand_identity.description: A clean-label food brand making real food — protein powders, protein bars, nut spreads, muesli and kids' nutrition — with every ingredient declared upfront.
brand_identity.mission: We're re-building the world's trust in food.

business_positioning.positioning_statement: We make food so clean, we can proudly declare every single ingredient that goes into it, upfront.

personas.description: Health-motivated shopper who has been burned by 'healthy' packaged food and now reads ingredient lists before buying.
goals: Find foods whose ingredient lists match the marketing claims
buying_triggers: Seeing a short, fully-declared ingredient list with percentages that add to 100%
relatable_situations: Standing in a store aisle squinting at the crimp of a pack to read ingredients

personas.description: Person who wants more protein but does not identify as a gym-goer, and is unsure whether protein products are 'for them'.
pain_points: Concerned about bloating, gas or acne from protein powders
relatable_situations: The 4pm slump and reaching for a fried snack

segments.description: Households replacing conventional packaged snacks, spreads and breakfast cereals with short-ingredient alternatives.

pain_points: Distrust of brands that hide ingredient lists in microscopic font at the back
desired_outcomes: A food where every ingredient is declared upfront and adds up to 100%
motivations: Rebuilding personal trust in packaged food after feeling lied to by 'healthy' claims
fears: Being sold lies in the name of 'healthy'
objections: Skepticism that any brand can be fully transparent
purchase_triggers: First purchase via small sampler packs or sachets
decision_criteria: Number and recognisability of ingredients (e.g. 'Just 5-7 ingredients')
emotional_benefits: Feeling respected as a reader rather than fooled
relatable_situations: The late-night dessert craving and reaching for a clean protein bar
emotional_triggers: Frustration at being fooled by 'healthy' marketing

brand_voice.language_style: Direct, conversational copy that names the problem and shows the ingredients.
example_phrases: Real food is flawed. And those flaws are perfect!

content_pillars: Declare it upfront: making the full ingredient list impossible to miss
Nothing to hide: inside the Bada Barkhana and the people who make the food
creative_angles: Contrast a squint-at-the-crimp label moment with a short ingredient list that adds to 100%
Show real food's 'flaws' (imperfect look) as proof of no tampering, side by side with the ingredient list
relatable_situations: Trying a sampler sachet before committing to a 1kg pack
